Far more serious: a domain one letter short of their name, mgmplumbingsuppies.com (no "l"), is live, parked, and running a US pay-per-call plumbing lead-generation page — advertising drain cleaning, clogged toilets, leaky taps and water-heater work, with a US freephone number and a disclaimer that it is "an independent marketing and referral platform", "not a direct service provider" and "not affiliated with" any business. research.summary: Small, dense, well-stocked plumbers' merchant at 66 Kenway Road, Earls Court SW5, with a genuinely exceptional reputation — 5.0 stars from 26 Google reviews, described by customers in unusually warm terms (one calls the staff "a huge asset to the area"). Despite that, they rank only #2 in the local pack, behind Hay Plumbing & Heating (4.7/14, three minutes away, which has a website). They are also a listed showroom partner of Ideal Bathrooms, implying specification work beyond the counter, with zero online reflection of that side of the business. The standout finding: a domain one letter short of their name (mgmplumbingsuppies.com) is live and running a US pay-per-call plumbing lead-generation page, and an unclaimed Birdeye profile publishes that typo domain as MGM's official website — while the correctly-spelled domains (mgmplumbingsupplies.com and .co.uk) appear to be unregistered. Unlike other prospects, their Google Business Profile is actively managed (updated by the business itself six weeks ago, correctly categorised as "Plumbers' merchant") — the usual free-gift openers (unclaimed listing, wrong category, early closing) do not apply here. The corporate picture is unusually unclear: the registered company (MGM Plumbing Supplies Ltd, 14156605) is administered from a residential address in Sutton, fifteen miles away, has had five officer resignations in four years, an overdue confirmation statement, and a change of sole director (Farid Haddour, appointed 2 Aug 2025) the same day a Tony Moussa resigned — who may or may not be the "Tony" customers name in reviews as the man behind the counter. A separately-incorporated business next door at 64 Kenway Road (MGM Electrical and Building Supplies, plus a property company, both run by Ahmad El Chama) may or may not be connected — the names and addresses align but the officers don't, so this is inference, not fact.

talkingPoints: There's a website using your name with one letter missing, and it's selling plumbing leads to somebody else. Birdeye's got it listed as your official site. I don't think you know.
The one with your name spelled properly looks like nobody's registered it. That's about a tenner a year. I'd rather you owned it than the bloke selling leads.
Search plumbers merchant round here — Hay come up above you. They're 4.7 from fourteen. You're 5.0 from twenty-six. The one thing they've got that you haven't is a website.
You've got a straight five out of five from twenty-six people. I look at a lot of these and almost nobody has that. And it exists in exactly one place.
Google says you shut at seven. Yell says five on one page and six on another. Someone's driving over at half five and finding you shut — or not coming because they think you are.
notes: REAL RESEARCH — sourced from Companies House, Google, Birdeye, Yell and Ideal Bathrooms, compiled 11 Sep 2026.

THIS PROSPECT IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHERS: the usual free-gift openers do NOT apply. Their Google listing is already claimed and actively managed, and their category is already correct ("Plumbers' merchant"). Never say the listing is unclaimed or the category is wrong — both are factually false here and will cost credibility immediately. The real free gifts here are: pointing out the correct domain looks unregistered, and offering to help get the contradictory opening hours corrected.

Ask for Tony — that's the name customers actually use in reviews. Whether he's the owner or not, he can tell you who is. Do NOT assume he's the owner or mention any company filings on the call. A "Tony Moussa" resigned as a director in August 2025 and may or may not be the same man — never reference this on the call.

The ownership picture is genuinely unclear — the registered director (Farid Haddour, appointed Aug 2025) is based in Sutton, not the shop, and there have been five officer resignations in four years. Treat the first call as DISCOVERY, not a pitch: the real goal of call one is a name, a role and a callback time — not a meeting. Qualify before pitching properly: ask whether it's their shop or whether they work for someone, before spending the domain finding on someone who can't buy.

There may be a connected business next door at 64 Kenway Road (MGM Electrical and Building Supplies, run by Ahmad El Chama, on-site) — but this is inference only, the officers don't match the plumbing company's. Ask carefully ("is the electrical place next door anything to do with you?"), never assert a connection. If confirmed, it's a separate, easier sale worth its own call — a brand-new business with no online presence at all.

Before dialling: confirm at a domain registrar whether mgmplumbingsupplies.co.uk is genuinely available and what it costs — a failed DNS lookup is strong evidence but not proof of availability, and the price must not be promised without checking. Also have on screen: the typo-domain lead-gen page, the Google result showing Hay ranking above MGM, and the two contradictory Yell closing times.
Best time to call: Tuesday–Thursday 09:30–10:30, or 14:00–15:30 (Google's popular-times data suggests this isn't a busy window). Avoid 07:00–09:00, the trade rush.

Honest odds from the research: roughly 8/10 chance of getting through (small shop, direct line, long hours), 4/10 of booking a meeting — but the realistic GOOD outcome of call one is a name, a role and a callback time, not a meeting itself. Only 3/10 of closing overall, the weakest of any prospect researched so far, because of the ownership uncertainty, not a weak pitch.
Never mention the £75/month or £50/month products on this call — this business has enough uncertainty already without adding a subscription to the decision.

In the wider pipeline this prospect was ranked behind The Plumbing Merchant (clearer buyer, clearer money) and ahead of Kenon — call this one as a discovery call, not expecting to close. Also worth a separate call: 64 Kenway Road, if it's genuinely a connected, brand-new business.

script.opening: Morning — is {{firstName}} about? ... You don't know me, and I'll be straight with you — this is a cold call, but I'd have rung you about this bit either way. Thirty seconds?
script.hook: There's a website live right now — mgmplumbingsuppies dot com, no L in "suppies". It's not yours. It's a parked page selling plumbing jobs on to some call centre, and there's a review site listing it as your official website.
script.valueStatement: What I do is small — one site with what you stock, your hours, your reviews on it, and your name pointing at you instead of at them. That's it — nothing you don't need.
script.demoOffer: Here's what I'd suggest. Two things you can do without me either way — the domain with your name spelled properly looks like nobody's registered it, so it's worth grabbing before the lead-gen lot do, and your opening hours are different across four different sites, which I'll get corrected where I can, no charge. On top of that, give me till Thursday and I'll build what your actual page would look like — your reviews, your name on it. Fifteen minutes on the phone, you look at the real thing, you tell me yes or no.
script.pricing: Four hundred pounds, one-off. Nothing monthly, no contract. You own it.

discovery.question: Is it your shop, or do you work for someone?
discovery.why: The qualifying question — get this before spending the domain finding on someone who can't buy. Ask it respectfully, not as an interrogation.
listenFor: "It's mine" opens the whole call up
"I just work here" — ask who'd be the person, and whether they're normally in during the week

discovery.question: How long's the shop been on Kenway Road?
discovery.why: Simple rapport opener while you're establishing who you're speaking to.
listenFor: Any long-tenure answer supports the "huge asset to the area" review theme later

discovery.question: Where does a new customer usually come from?
discovery.why: Sets up the Hay comparison — if the answer is search or passing trade, the ranking gap becomes directly relevant.
listenFor: "They just find us" or "word gets round" both hand you the Hay-outranking line

discovery.question: Do you do much bathroom work, or is it mostly parts?
discovery.why: Confirms whether the Ideal Bathrooms showroom side is real before asserting it matters.
listenFor: Any real bathroom volume supports leading with the showroom-is-invisible angle

discovery.question: Do people ever ring to check you're open?
discovery.why: Makes the four-different-opening-hours problem concrete in his own words.
listenFor: "All the time" is the value statement written for you

discovery.question: Do you ever get calls that clearly meant somebody else?
discovery.why: May surface the typo-domain confusion from their own side without you having to lead with it.
listenFor: Any mention of odd or American-sounding enquiries could be lead-gen overflow from the parked domain

extraObjections.objection: Our customers are plumbers, they don't browse.
extraObjections.meaning: True of the trade counter, not necessarily true of the showroom side he's also part of.
extraObjections.response: The trade don't, you're right. But you're listed with Ideal Bathrooms — is there a bathroom side? Because that customer absolutely does, and she won't find you at all.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Suppose there is, a bit. / Not really, no.
extraObjections.followUp: If there's real bathroom volume, ask the showroom discovery question directly.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If there's genuinely no showroom trade worth mentioning, don't push that angle — fall back to the domain and the Hay comparison.

extraObjections.objection: The owner's not here / he's not in much.
extraObjections.meaning: A route, not a brush-off. Get a way to reach him rather than accepting the dead end.
extraObjections.response: Fair enough. Best way to reach him — does he come in, or is there a number? I'd rather five minutes with him than keep bothering you.
extraObjections.likelyReply: He's usually in Tuesdays. / I can take a message.
extraObjections.followUp: Confirm exactly when he's normally in, or take a direct number if offered.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If no route is offered after asking once, thank them and try the shop again another day rather than pressing.

extraObjections.objection: We get ten of you a week.
extraObjections.meaning: Fatigue with generic cold callers, not a rejection of this specific finding. Prove you're different, checkably.
extraObjections.response: I know, and they all say the same thing. I'm ringing because someone's running a lead-gen site off your name. Type mgmplumbingsuppies dot com — no L in suppies — while I'm on the phone.
extraObjections.likelyReply: (They check, and see it.) / Bloody hell, that's mine near enough.
extraObjections.followUp: Once they've seen it, move straight into the Hay comparison and the free domain-registration tip.
extraObjections.whenToStop: Only offer this if you're confident the typo domain is still live — check before the call, not during it.

extraObjections.objection: Who else have you built for?
extraObjections.meaning: A reference check. Never invent a client — a fabricated reference is fatal if checked.
extraObjections.response: Straight answer — I'm early on, so you'd be one of the first, which is exactly why you'd get proper attention instead of being file number forty. Let me build yours and show you before you pay anything.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Fair enough. / I'd rather see something first.
extraObjections.followUp: Move straight to the demo offer — the work is the reference.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If they insist on seeing existing client work you don't have, be honest you don't have it yet rather than stretching the truth.

extraObjections.objection: Can you just sort the domain and leave it there?
extraObjections.meaning: A genuine, smaller ask. Say yes properly — it's the best way to earn the second conversation.
extraObjections.response: Absolutely, and I'd rather you did that than nothing. I'll walk you through registering it yourself so it's in your name, not mine. If you want the site later you know where I am.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Yeah, go on then. / Appreciate that, actually.
extraObjections.followUp: Actually walk them through it, or send clear steps — then leave the site conversation open, don't chase it.
extraObjections.whenToStop: Never turn this into a pitch. A prospect helped for free converts later far more often than one who feels squeezed.

extraObjections.objection: We're not doing Facebook and all that.
extraObjections.meaning: A pre-emptive objection to something you were never suggesting. Agree immediately.
extraObjections.response: Nor would I bother in your line. I'm not suggesting it — this is just so people searching for you find you rather than Hay.
extraObjections.followUp: Return to the Hay comparison or the domain point immediately.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — should resolve in one line.

extraObjections.meaning: A comparison against the wrong rival — Screwfix isn't who's actually beating them in search.
extraObjections.response: You can't and you shouldn't. I'm not worried about Screwfix — I'm worried about Hay three minutes up the road, because they're the one actually taking your searches.
extraObjections.followUp: Move straight into the 5.0-vs-4.7 numbers if they haven't landed yet.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — this should redirect the conversation, not end it.

customNodes.coach: Do not skip the qualifying question. Ask it before you go any further: "Is this your shop, or do you work for someone?" You need that answer before you spend the domain finding on someone who can't say yes.

customNodes.theySay: We're on Google already, we're fine.
customNodes.whatISay: You are, and you look after it properly — most don't. But Hay up on Earls Court Road come above you and they're rated lower than you. Google's page can't fix that on its own.
customNodes.goal: Give real credit for the well-managed listing, then show the specific thing it can't do.

customNodes.whatISay: Maybe not. But there's already a site using your name with a letter missing, selling plumbing jobs to someone else's call centre. That's happening whether you want a website or not.
customNodes.goal: Don't argue the need for a website — lead with the active harm instead. The free-category-fix gift doesn't exist here, so don't reach for it.

customNodes.whatISay: I'd expect so with a five-star rating. This isn't about the regulars — it's about the bloke who's new to the area and searches, and gets Hay first.
customNodes.goal: Agree completely, then narrow to the customer who doesn't exist yet: the one who searches instead of asking around.

customNodes.whatISay: {{callerName}}, I run a small outfit called {{brand}} — I build websites for local businesses. I'm one person, not an agency. I rang because of the domain thing, which I'd have told you about either way.
customNodes.goal: Answer straight and short. The domain finding is real regardless of whether they buy — say so plainly.

customNodes.whatISay: Fair enough. Then do the cheap bit first — register your own domain before someone else does, it's about a tenner. That's not me selling you anything. The site can wait till it suits you.
customNodes.goal: Split the ask. Offering the free, tiny action first keeps the relationship alive and makes you credible.

customNodes.whatISay: Course. I'll send you the link to that lead-generation site using your name — you'll want to see it. Best address? And I'll ring Thursday about half ten.
customNodes.goal: Accept the email request, but attach the actual evidence and a named follow-up time.

customNodes.whatISay: No problem. When's your quiet bit — first thing before the trade come in, or mid-afternoon? I'll ring then, four minutes.
customNodes.goal: Believe them and book a specific, informed time — 09:30–10:30 is usually the gap after the 7am trade rush.

customNodes.theySay: I'm not the owner, I just work here.
customNodes.whatISay: No problem at all. Can I tell you the reason I rang, and you can decide whether it's worth passing on? There's a website using your name that isn't yours. Who'd be the person — and are they in during the week?
customNodes.goal: Recruit whoever answered as an ally, not an obstacle. Your goal is a name and a route, not a pitch to the wrong person.

customNodes.whatISay: Most don't. But you weren't sitting on five out of five from twenty-six people then, and there wasn't someone squatting on your name. The situation's different now even if the idea isn't.
customNodes.goal: Separate the old attempt from now — the evidence and the domain threat are both new.

customNodes.theySay: Who's going to look after it?
customNodes.whatISay: Nobody — it's built so it doesn't need looking after. What you stock, your hours, your reviews, your phone number. Set up once. Anything changes, you ring me.
customNodes.goal: Remove the imagined ongoing work entirely.

customNodes.theySay: I'll have to speak to someone about it.
customNodes.whatISay: Of course. Would it help if I built it first so there's something real to show rather than a description? Costs nothing to look at, and it's a much easier conversation than 'a bloke rang'.
customNodes.goal: Entirely plausible given how unclear ownership is here — make it easy to pass on, don't push for a name.

customNodes.whatISay: No problem. Can I do one thing — I'll send the link to that site using your name today, and ring you Tuesday. If it's a no then, that's the end of it and you won't hear from me again.
customNodes.goal: Never accept open-ended. Send the evidence today regardless, and pin a specific day to follow up.

customNodes.whatISay: Course. Is first thing before the trade come in any good, or mid-afternoon — around two, half two? Either's fine my end.
customNodes.goal: Offer specific, informed times — the known quiet windows around the 07:00 opening and the early afternoon.

customNodes.whatISay: No problem at all. Tuesday to Thursday, morning around half nine or early afternoon usually suits best from what I understand — does either work, or is there a better day?
customNodes.goal: Pin a specific day and time using what's already known about the quieter parts of their day.
